display.title: Episode 216: Reb Ariel and the Lion (Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini, Uncle Yossi shows off the mezuzah contest winners in the new newsletter, and a girl tells her mother how a lion guarded Rabbi Ariel for keeping Shabbos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini. Uncle Yossi opens with the new Tzivos Hashem newsletter, free for members, and walks listeners through page two, where the grand winners of his mezuzah drawing contest appear, ending with a drawing that shows where the Torah commands us to put a mezuzah on our doorposts. Since Adar has begun again, it is time to add even more joy, so everyone joins the Hakochainik march. A boy visiting from Ann Arbor, Michigan recites the Shema. Story time: on a Friday afternoon, little Devorah hurries home to help her mother prepare for Shabbos and retells her teacher's story. Rabbi Ariel joined a caravan through the wilderness on condition that it would rest on Shabbos, but the travelers laughed and moved on without him. As Shabbos began, a huge lion came and stood guard over him all Shabbos, then carried him through the night to the caravan, which had been attacked by wild animals. The travelers asked forgiveness and made him their leader.
display.lesson: Whoever guards the Shabbos is guarded by the Shabbos.

date.note: 'Today is Rosh Chodesh, Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini' (first day, 30 Adar I, a Tuesday). Matches the weekly estimate.
